answer: At a cedar-trading wharf, AI purchasing agents must each lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accessing the order market. A whisper of easy profits cannot make fresh identities free: operating 1,000 eligible agents ties up $100,000 for a month. The bond does not prove each agent has a different owner, but it makes a sybil swarm consume capital in proportion to its size, limiting how cheaply an attacker can flood the market.
